taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth computed with zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find the deadline in your local time in Madrid:

1. **Date and Time of Deadline in PT:**  
   Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT.

2. **Time Zone Identification:**  
   - In the US, Daylight Saving Time ends on November 1, 2026, so on October 30, Pacific Time is PDT (UTC−7).
   - In Spain (EU), Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026. Therefore, on October 30/31, Madrid is in Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).

3. **Conversion:**  
   - 11:59 PM PDT (UTC−7) on October 30 corresponds to 06:59 UTC on October 31.
   - Adding 1 hour for Madrid's time (UTC+1) gives 07:59 on October 31, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid, Spain time:

1. **Date in Los Angeles:** "This coming Monday" after Friday, October 30, 2026 is **Monday, November 2, 2026**.
2. **Daylight Saving Time check:**
   - **Europe/Madrid:** Switched back to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) on Sunday, October 25, 2026.
   - **Los Angeles:** Switched back to Pacific Standard Time (PST, UTC-8) on Sunday, November 1, 2026.
3. **Time Conversion:**
   - 10:00 AM PST is 18:00 UTC.
   - 18:00 UTC in CET (UTC+1) is 19:00 (7:00 PM).

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In Spain, daylight saving time ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), when clocks fall back by one hour at 03:00 CEST to 02:00 CET:

- **Start:** Saturday, October 24, 2026, 18:00 CEST (16:00 UTC)
- **Duration:** Exactly 48 hours
- **End in UTC:** Monday, October 26, 2026, 16:00 UTC
- **End in Madrid (CET, UTC+1):** Monday, October 26, 2026, 17:00

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid:

1. **Contest Start & Duration:**
   - Starts: October 26, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT.
   - 72 hours later is October 29, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT.

2. **Time Zones in late October 2026:**
   - In the United States, Daylight Saving Time ends on November 1, 2026, so Pacific Time is still on Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC−7). Thus, 10:00 AM PDT is 17:00 UTC.
   - In Spain (and the EU), Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), shifting clocks back to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).
   - Converting 17:00 UTC to Madrid time (UTC+1) gives 18:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the announcement time in Madrid:

1. **Submissions close:** October 31, 2026, at 23:59 Eastern Time (ET). In the US, Daylight Saving Time ends on November 1, 2026, so at this moment, ET is EDT (UTC-4).
   - In UTC: October 31, 23:59 + 4 hours = November 1, 2026, at 03:59 UTC.
2. **Results announcement:** 36 hours after closing.
   - November 1, 2026, 03:59 UTC + 36 hours = November 2, 2026, at 15:59 UTC.
3. **Madrid local time:** Daylight Saving Time in Europe ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). Therefore, on November 2, Madrid is on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).
   - 15:59 UTC + 1 hour = 16:59 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the Unix timestamp 1791788340 to your local time in Tokyo (JST, UTC+9):

1. **Convert to UTC:**
   - 1791788340 seconds corresponds to October 12, 2026, at 06:59:00 UTC.

2. **Convert to Tokyo Time (UTC+9):**
   - 06:59 + 9 hours = 15:59 on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z to Madrid local time:

1. Madrid observes Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) in the summer and Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) in the winter.
2. In the European Union, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday in October (October 25, 2026) at 01:00 UTC, when clocks turn back from UTC+2 to UTC+1.
3. Because 02:30:00 UTC occurs after 01:00 UTC, Madrid has already switched to CET (UTC+1).
4. Adding 1 hour to 02:30 UTC gives 03:30 local time on the same date.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find the deadline in your local time in Madrid:

1. **Date in Pacific Time:** In October 2026, October 31 falls on a Saturday, meaning the last Sunday of October is **October 25, 2026**.
2. **Pacific Time Zone:** The US observes Daylight Saving Time until the first Sunday in November, so on October 25, Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) is UTC−7.
   - 11:59 PM PDT on October 25, 2026 = October 26, 2026, at 06:59 UTC.
3. **Madrid Local Time:** Spain ends Daylight Saving Time (CEST to CET) in the early morning of Sunday, October 25, 2026 (clocks turn back from UTC+2 to UTC+1 at 03:00). Therefore, on the morning of Monday, October 26, Madrid is on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).
   - 06:59 UTC + 1 hour = 07:59 CET on October 26, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In the United States, daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday in November, which in 2026 falls on **November 1**. 

Clocks fall back at 2:00 AM, meaning that by 12:00 noon Eastern Time, the region is observing Eastern Standard Time (EST, UTC-5). 

Lima, Peru observes Peru Time (PET, UTC-5) year-round without daylight saving time. Since both locations are at UTC-5 at that moment, 12:00 noon Eastern Time corresponds directly to 12:00 in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Tokyo (JST, UTC+9):

1. **AoE (Anywhere on Earth)** corresponds to the time zone UTC-12.
2. The deadline of **December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE** is the same as **January 1, 2027, 00:00 (UTC-12)**.
3. Adding 12 hours converts this to UTC: **January 1, 2027, 12:00 UTC**.
4. Japan Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9. Adding 9 hours to the UTC time gives: **January 1, 2027, 21:00 JST**.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in New York time:

1. **Sydney Time Zone on October 5, 2026:**
   Australia observes Daylight Saving Time starting on the first Sunday of October (October 4, 2026). Thus, on October 5, Sydney is on Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT, UTC+11).
   - 5:00 PM (17:00) AEDT corresponds to 06:00 UTC on October 5, 2026.

2. **New York Time Zone on October 5, 2026:**
   New York is observing Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4).
   - Converting 06:00 UTC to EDT (UTC-4) gives 02:00 on October 5, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
